Summary With South Korea's popular fashion and beauty brands expanding their reach, several have established a presence in Malaysian malls.
 Notable entries include casualwear label TOPTEN10, which opened outlets in Sunway Pyramid and 1 Utama, and the anticipated arrival of Musinsa Standard following its distribution agreement with Mitra Adiperkasa.
 In fashion accessories, Stand Oil has opened a boutique in Pavilion Kuala Lumpur.
 The Korean beauty scene thrives with Shinsegae Hyperground's pop-up and Olive Young's collaboration with Sephora, while Tamburins plans to open a boutique in Suria KLCC.

By Malay Mail First Published: Monday, 09 Nov 2026 4:40 PM MYT Last Modified: Tuesday, 10 Nov 2026 8:20 AM MYT × Subscribe to Newsletter
 Subscribe KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Forget saving space in your suitcase for that next Seoul shopping spree. Some of South Korea’s coolest fashion and beauty labels are bringing the goods straight to Malaysia.
 From minimalist wardrobe staples and cult handbags to perfumes that double as art objects, a fresh wave of Korean brands have made its way into Malaysian malls in 2026, with more arrivals on the horizon.
 Here are the names worth knowing.
 The wardrobe refresh 
 South Korean casualwear label TOPTEN10 made its Malaysian debut at Sunway Pyramid in January, followed by a second outlet at 1 Utama in July.
 Think relaxed silhouettes, fuss-free basics and easy layering pieces that would look right at home in a K-drama airport scene.
 Founded in 2012, the brand offers an affordable alternative for shoppers who prefer understated everyday fashion without the flashy logos.
 And it has company on the way.
         View this post on Instagram                       A post shared by @topten10_malaysia 
 Musinsa Standard, the in-house label of South Korean fashion platform Musinsa, is preparing to enter Malaysia after securing an exclusive distribution agreement with retail group Mitra Adiperkasa (MAP) in August.
 Known for its contemporary essentials and minimalist streetwear, the label plans to open stores in Kuala Lumpur and other major Malaysian cities, although dates and locations have yet to be announced.
 The expansion follows impressive online demand from Malaysian shoppers, with Musinsa reporting average annual transaction volume growth of 63 per cent between 2023 and 2025 on its global store, followed by a 117 per cent year-on-year surge in the first half of 2026.
 Clearly, Malaysians have been doing their Korean fashion homework.
         View this post on Instagram                       A post shared by 무신사 스탠다드 | musinsa standard (@musinsa_standard) 
 The bag obsession 
 If your social media feed has been serving up effortlessly cool Korean handbags, chances are Stand Oil has made an appearance.
 Founded in Seoul in 2018, the accessories label has built a following with its sleek shoulder bags, retro-inspired shapes and playful proportions.
 Its appeal lies in handbags that feel both practical and fashion-forward, with enough personality to make even a basic jeans-and-T-shirt combination look intentional.
 And there is no need to order from overseas. Stand Oil now has a boutique on Level 4 of Pavilion Kuala Lumpur, allowing shoppers to check out the bags in person.
         View this post on Instagram                       A post shared by STAND OIL / 스탠드오일 (@standoil) 
 The beauty takeover 
 No Korean shopping story would be complete without K-beauty, and Malaysia’s skincare obsession shows little sign of slowing down.
 Among the latest arrivals is Shinsegae Hyperground, the South Korean retail giant’s pop-up platform, which has opened at Seibu in The Exchange TRX.
 Running until March 2027, the space will feature a rotating selection of more than 10 Korean fashion and beauty labels, including Dinto, Headspa7, Fivebybe, Marie Claire and Tansanmagnesium.
         View this post on Instagram                       A post shared by 我是咸鱼！咸鱼就是我 (@saltedfish.ying) 
 Meanwhile, Malaysian beauty retailer HERMO has returned to bricks-and-mortar shopping with a store at The Campus in Ampang, bringing together Korean skincare and cosmetics in a space designed for browsing and discovering new products.
 There is also Olive Young, the Korean beauty powerhouse that has become practically compulsory on Seoul shopping itineraries.
 Rather than opening a standalone Malaysian store, the retailer has partnered with Sephora to bring a curated selection of Korean beauty brands to local shoppers, with a dedicated discovery space launched at Fahrenheit88 in September.
 Sight and scent 
 South Korean eyewear label Gentle Monster opened its second and largest Malaysian flagship at Suria KLCC in May 2026, following its debut at The Exchange TRX.
         View this post on Instagram                       A post shared by Nilofer - Singapore | Travel | Food | UGC (@niloferreshma) 
 Known for its futuristic frames and boundary-pushing retail concepts, the brand has turned its latest boutique into something of an art installation, complete with a kinetic display of three giant moving heads that blink, shift their gaze and change expressions.
 Located on the mall’s ground floor, the store brings together fashion, technology and contemporary art, proving that shopping for sunglasses can be quite the spectacle.
 And the creative connection doesn’t end there. Tamburins, the cult Korean fragrance label from the same company behind Gentle Monster, is also preparing to open its first Malaysian boutique at Suria KLCC.
         View this post on Instagram                       A post shared by TAMBURINS 탬버린즈 (@tamburinsofficial) 
 Known for sculptural perfume bottles, unconventional fragrances and stores that resemble contemporary art galleries, Tamburins has made beauty products feel like fashion accessories.
 Its celebrity connections have only added to the hype, with campaigns featuring Blackpink’s Jennie, Stray Kids’ Felix and actor Byeon Woo-seok.
 The label is preparing to open its first Malaysian boutique at Suria KLCC, although an official opening date has yet to be announced.
